subject: POC Trial: model selection & success criteria
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@acme.com>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: POC Trial: model selection & success criteria

Hi Carlos / Priya,

Great to meet earlier — thanks for the time. Quick recap + proposed next steps for the POC/trial so we can lock scope and timeline. Please confirm or flag edits.

Summary of needs from today's call:
- Primary use: clinical triage assistant for intake forms (free-text)
- Expected volume: ~5000 requests/day during pilot, spikes to 15k/day
- Multilingual: English priority, Spanish + French coverage required
- Compliance: data residency in US, audit logs required

Proposed success criteria (candidate metrics):
1) Precision/QA: >= 85% accuracy on labeled triage tests (we'll provide labeling rubric)
2) Latency: 95th percentile < 300ms for generation (token-limited responses)
3) Hallucination: < 5% critical hallucination rate on safety prompt-set
4) Multilingual parity: Spanish/French not to degrade more than 10% vs English on core intents
5) Reliability: 99.5% API availability during trial window

Evaluation plan (high level):
- Redwood provides a test harness + seeded prompt set (we can start with 1k sample queries)
- Phase 1 (Week 1): integration + smoke tests with small subset (50 req/s)
- Phase 2 (Week 2): full-run evaluation, load tests, user acceptance testing with your QA team
- Deliverables: evaluation report, per-intent confusion matrix, latency/throughput charts

Model recommendations for the trial (open models):
- Primary: Llama-2-Chat-70B (fp16) — best balance of instruction-following and safety for triage prompts
- Fallback: Llama-2-Chat-13B (int8 quantized) — keeps latency/cost predictable under load and for smaller on-prem nodes
- Alternative lightweight: Mistral-Instruct-34B (if you want better cost/latency trade-offs for non-critical paths)

Notes on multilingual: we recommend fine-tuning or prompt-enrichment for Spanish/French examples and adding a small translated seed set (we can coordinate).

Proposed timeline (stretch): 2-week pilot starting once mutual action plan signed:
- Week 0 (this week): agree success criteria, share test data and POC owners
- Week 1: integration + developer validation
- Week 2: evaluation + UAT + review

Ownership:
- Redwood SE: Marissa Cole (I'll loop her in for technical setup)
- Redwood AE: Ben Carter (commercial point)
- Acme POC owner: please confirm who owns the trial on your side (product/technical)

Next steps:
1) Confirm acceptance criteria + POC owner on your side
2) Share the initial seed dataset (we can accept a redacted CSV)
3) Align on target start date (suggest week of Sep 6)

I'll prep the POC plan doc and share templates (success criteria spreadsheet + evaluation harness).

Thanks,

Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198

From: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@acme.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: POC Trial: model selection & success criteria

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. This aligns closely with what we discussed. A few clarifications/requests from our side:

1) Success criteria weighting: we care most about safety/hallucination and accuracy on clinical intents. Latency is important but we can relax to 95th < 400ms if needed during the first run.
2) Hallucination thresholds: can you include a short definition and example-based check in the evaluation (critical vs non-critical hallucinations)?
3) Data residency: must remain in US regions for the pilot. Please confirm Redwood can guarantee region-specific routing + logs for audit.
4) POC owner: Priya Desai (Product Manager) will own product-side coordination. I'll be available for weekly syncs.

We have an internal QA set of ~800 labeled examples in English and ~200 translated to Spanish. We'll share redacted CSV by end of day Wednesday.

If Redwood can confirm the US-only routing and include hallucination checks in the evaluation plan, we can aim to start the week of Sep 6. Also ok with the primary model choice — please include a lower-cost fallback for load testing.

Best,
Carlos Vega
Head of Product — Acme Health
carlos.vega@acme.com

Marissa — forwarding the thread. Acme (Carlos + Priya) confirmed POC owner (Priya) and asked for US-only routing and hallucination checks. They have ~1k labeled examples (800 English, 200 Spanish) to share by Wednesday.

Can you: 
- Draft the POC plan doc (template attached when ready)
- Prepare an evaluation harness that includes hallucination checkpoints (critical vs non-critical)
- Pre-configure two model variants: Llama-2-Chat-70B (primary) and Llama-2-Chat-13B int8 (fallback) and validate US-region deployment
- Suggest a reasonable cost/throughput config for Redwood Dedicated vs Hosted for this pilot (estimations only)

Let's aim to have a kickoff calendar invite for Sep 6. Ben — flag commercial items if anything looks off.

Thanks,
Jordan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC Trial: model selection & success criteria

Thanks — I'm on it. High-level POC plan and technical notes below; I'll attach the POC-Plan-Acme.docx and the Success Criteria spreadsheet once they're finalized.

POC Plan (concise):
- Kickoff (Sep 6): 30–45m technical + success criteria alignment with Acme (Jordan, Ben, Priya, Carlos, Marissa)
- Week 1 (Sep 7–13): Integration + smoke tests
  - Redwood will provision US-region hosted endpoints pinned to Llama-2-Chat-70B (primary) and Llama-2-Chat-13B int8 (fallback)
  - We'll provide a dockerized evaluation harness and example scripts to run locally or in their CI
  - Add instrumentation hooks for audit logs and token-level cost tracing
- Week 2 (Sep 14–20): Full evaluation + load tests + UAT
  - Run seeded evaluation across English/Spanish sets (we'll add a short FR subset if they provide)
  - Metrics: accuracy, per-intent precision/recall, critical-hallucination rate, latency p50/p95, error rates
  - Deliverable: evaluation report + recommended rollout config (quantization, batching)

Model selection rationale:
- Llama-2-Chat-70B (fp16): best baseline for instruction-following and clinical intent fidelity. Good for initial accuracy-focused runs.
- Llama-2-Chat-13B (int8 quant): fallback for load and cost control; acceptable trade-off for non-critical flows and burst capacity.
- If we need further latency reduction, we can run a smaller Mistral variant for background tasks.

Multilingual plan:
- We'll run the provided Spanish samples during both smoke and full evaluation. For French, suggest a small 100-example set — optional but recommended.
- Prompt templates will include language tags and light prompt engineering to reduce hallucination.

Hallucination checks:
- We'll include a labeled safety set and a checkpoint that flags responses with low factuality scores using an ensemble of model-based QA checks (we'll provide the script).
- We'll categorize hallucinations as Critical (affects clinical triage outcome) vs Non-critical; evaluation will report both rates.

Attachments I'll upload + share to the drive: POC-Plan-Acme.docx, POC-Success-Criteria.xlsx, Evaluation-Seed-Prompts.csv

Immediate ask from us:
- Acme: confirm Priya Desai as POC owner (they already did) and share the redacted CSV by Wed EOD
- Jordan/Ben: confirm kickoff time on Sep 6 (morning PST preferred)

I'll prepare the environment and a quick runbook for data redaction/ingest. Also confirming US-region routing and audit logs — we have region pinning and per-request audit logging available for hosted trials (I will include the configuration steps in the POC doc).

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
